records.source: מִזְמ֗וֹר לְדָ֫וִ֥דיְהוָ֤ה׀שְׁמַ֬ע תְּפִלָּתִ֗י הַאֲזִ֥ינָה אֶל־תַּחֲנוּנַ֑י בֶּאֱמֻנָתְךָ֥ עֲ֝נֵ֗נִי בְּצִדְקָתֶֽךָ׃
records.gloss: A psalm of David. YHWH, hear my prayer; give ear to my supplications; in your faithfulness answer me, in your righteousness.
pieces: A psalm of David. {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, hear my prayer; listen as I plead for mercy. Answer me in {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} faithfulness and in {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} righteousness.

L.1: A psalm of David. {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, hear my prayer; give ear to my pleas for mercy; in {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} faithfulness answer me, in {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} righteousness.

R.1: A song of David. {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, hear my prayer. Listen when I beg {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} for help. Answer me, because {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} are faithful and {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} do what is right.

decisions.choice: The title shares verse 1
decisions.reason: As in 141:1, the short title and the first line are counted together as verse 1.

decisions.choice: your faithfulness, your righteousness: God's own character
decisions.reason: The psalmist appeals to what God is: faithful to his promises ('emunah) and righteous (tsedaqah), the one who sets things right for those who trust him (31:2; 71:2). He does not appeal to his own righteousness (verse 2).

decisions.choice: the last of the seven penitential psalms
decisions.reason: From early times the church has read Psalms 6, 32, 38, 51, 102, 130 and 143 as psalms of repentance.

decisions.choice: song
decisions.reason: As in 3:1.

decisions.choice: because you are faithful and you do what is right
alternatives: in your faithfulness, in your righteousness
decisions.reason: Readable turns the nouns into plain statements about God (m2).

records.heading: Do not bring your servant to trial

records.source: וְאַל־תָּב֣וֹא בְ֭מִשְׁפָּט אֶת־עַבְדֶּ֑ךָ כִּ֤י לֹֽא־יִצְדַּ֖ק לְפָנֶ֣יךָ כָל־חָֽי׃
records.gloss: And do not enter into judgment with your servant, for not is righteous before you any living.
pieces: Do not bring {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} servant to trial, for no living person can be found in the right before {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}.

L.2: And do not enter into judgment with {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} servant, for no one living is righteous before {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}.

R.2: Please do not take me to court and judge me. I am {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} servant. No one alive is innocent in {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} eyes.

decisions.choice: Romans 3:20; Galatians 2:16
decisions.reason: Paul echoes this line when he says that no one will be declared righteous before God by doing what the law requires (Romans 3:20; Galatians 2:16).

decisions.choice: enter into judgment: take to court
decisions.reason: The picture is of a lawsuit, with God as the one who brings the case (Job 9:32; 22:4; Isaiah 3:14).

decisions.choice: be righteous: be in the right, be found innocent
decisions.reason: The verb (tsadaq) is the language of the court: to be in the right, to win the case (51:6; Job 9:2).

decisions.choice: innocent
decisions.reason: Readable gives the court sense of the word (m3).

records.source: כִּ֥י רָ֘דַ֤ף אוֹיֵ֨ב׀נַפְשִׁ֗י דִּכָּ֣א לָ֭אָרֶץ חַיָּתִ֑י הוֹשִׁיבַ֥נִי בְ֝מַחֲשַׁכִּ֗ים כְּמֵתֵ֥י עוֹלָֽם׃
records.gloss: For he has pursued, [the] enemy, my soul; he has crushed to the ground my life; he has made me dwell in dark places like [the] dead of long ago.
pieces: The enemy has hunted me down and ground my life into the dust; he has left me to live in dark places, like people dead for ages.

L.3: For [the] enemy has pursued my soul; he has crushed my life to the ground; he has made me dwell in dark places like the dead of long ago.

R.3: My enemy has chased me and beaten me down to the ground. He makes me live in darkness, as if I had died long ago.

decisions.choice: like the dead of long ago: Lamentations 3:6
decisions.reason: Lamentations 3:6 uses the same words: "he has made me dwell in dark places like the dead of long ago".

decisions.choice: dark places: the darkness of the grave, or a dark hiding place
decisions.reason: Darkness is the place of the dead (88:7, 13). The psalmist feels as good as buried.

decisions.choice: the enemy: one enemy, or enemies as a group
decisions.reason: The enemy is singular, but verses 9 and 12 speak of enemies in the plural.

records.source: וַתִּתְעַטֵּ֣ף עָלַ֣י רוּחִ֑י בְּ֝תוֹכִ֗י יִשְׁתּוֹמֵ֥ם לִבִּֽי׃
records.gloss: And it faints upon me, my spirit; in my midst is appalled my heart.
pieces: My spirit sinks within me, and my heart is stunned inside me.

L.4: So my spirit grows faint within me; in my midst my heart is appalled.

R.4: I feel weak and ready to give up. Deep inside I am in shock.

decisions.choice: faints
decisions.reason: As in 142:4 (hit'attef).

decisions.choice: is appalled: is stunned, numb with horror
decisions.reason: The verb (shamem) is to be desolate or stunned, too shocked to act.

decisions.choice: I feel weak and ready to give up
decisions.reason: Readable says what the fainting spirit means in plain words.

records.source: זָ֘כַ֤רְתִּי יָמִ֨ים׀מִקֶּ֗דֶם הָגִ֥יתִי בְכָל־פָּעֳלֶ֑ךָ בְּֽמַעֲשֵׂ֖ה יָדֶ֣יךָ אֲשׂוֹחֵֽחַ׃
records.gloss: I remember days from long ago; I meditate on all your doing; on [the] work of your hands I muse.
pieces: I recall the days long past; I think over all that {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have done and reflect on what {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} hands have made.

L.5: I remember [the] days of old; I meditate on all {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} doing; on [the] work of {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} hands I ponder.

R.5: I remember what happened long ago. I think about all that {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have done. I think hard about the great things {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have done with {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} own hands.

decisions.choice: remembering the days of old: as in Psalm 77
decisions.reason: Psalm 77 also turns from despair to remembering God's deeds of long ago (77:6, 12-13), using the same words.

decisions.choice: meditate: think over, murmur to oneself
decisions.reason: As in 1:2, the verb (hagah) is to murmur or think something over.

decisions.choice: the work of your hands: what God has done
decisions.reason: This can be God's creation (8:7; 102:26) or his saving acts for his people (92:5). Here, with "days of old", it is most likely his deeds in Israel's past.

records.source: פֵּרַ֣שְׂתִּי יָדַ֣י אֵלֶ֑יךָ נַפְשִׁ֓י׀כְּאֶֽרֶץ־עֲיֵפָ֖ה לְךָ֣ סֶֽלָה׃
records.gloss: I spread out my hands to you; my soul like a land weary [is] for you. Selah.
pieces: I hold out my hands to {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}; my whole being waits for {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} like ground worn out by drought. Selah

L.6: I have spread out my hands to {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}; my soul [is] like a weary land for {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}. Selah

R.6: I reach out my hands to {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} in prayer. I need {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} the way dry land needs rain. Selah

decisions.choice: spreading out the hands: a gesture of prayer
decisions.reason: The hands were held out with palms open toward God (44:21; 88:10; 141:2).

decisions.choice: like a weary land: longing for God as dry ground longs for rain
decisions.reason: The same picture is in 63:2: a dry, exhausted land without water. The psalmist thirsts for God.

decisions.choice: worn out by drought (B); the way dry land needs rain (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what makes the land weary, so that the picture of thirst is clear (m2).

decisions.choice: Selah: a word whose meaning is no longer known
alternatives: lift up (the voice or the music)
decisions.reason: Selah stands at the end of a line 71 times in the Psalms and 3 times in Habakkuk 3. It is probably a direction for singing or music, perhaps a pause or an interlude; the ancient Greek translation renders it with a word meaning "interlude". It is not part of what is said, and here it marks a break after the line.

decisions.choice: Selah, kept as it is
decisions.reason: Its meaning is unknown (see the meaning decision on Selah), so every level keeps the word rather than guess, and keeps it apart from the sentence.

records.source: מַ֘הֵ֤ר עֲנֵ֨נִי׀יְהוָה֮ כָּלְתָ֪ה ר֫וּחִ֥י אַל־תַּסְתֵּ֣ר פָּנֶ֣יךָ מִמֶּ֑נִּי וְ֝נִמְשַׁ֗לְתִּי עִם־יֹ֥רְדֵי בֽוֹר׃
records.gloss: Quickly answer me, YHWH; it is spent, my spirit. Do not hide your face from me, or I will be like those going down [to the] pit.
pieces: {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, hurry and answer me; my spirit is failing. Do not keep {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} face hidden from me, or I will become one of those who sink into the pit.

L.7: Quickly answer me, {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}; my spirit is spent. Do not hide {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} face from me, or I will become like those who go down [to the] pit.

R.7: {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, answer me quickly. I cannot hold on much longer. Do not turn away from me, or I will die like everyone who goes down to the grave.

decisions.choice: hide your face: turn away, withhold help
decisions.reason: God's face turned toward someone means favor; hidden, it means he seems absent (13:2; 27:9; 102:3).

decisions.choice: those who go down to the pit: as in 28:1
decisions.reason: The same words close 28:1. The pit is the grave, the way down to the dead (30:4; 88:5).

decisions.choice: I cannot hold on much longer
decisions.reason: Readable says what the failing spirit means in plain words.

decisions.choice: do not turn away from me
decisions.reason: Readable explains the idiom (m1).

records.source: הַשְׁמִ֘יעֵ֤נִי בַבֹּ֨קֶר׀חַסְדֶּךָ֮ כִּֽי־בְךָ֪ בָ֫טָ֥חְתִּי הוֹדִיעֵ֗נִי דֶּֽרֶךְ־ז֥וּ אֵלֵ֑ךְ כִּֽי־אֵ֝לֶיךָ נָשָׂ֥אתִי נַפְשִֽׁי׃
records.gloss: Make me hear in the morning your loyal love, for in you I have trusted; make known to me [the] way which I should walk, for to you I lift up my soul.
pieces: Each morning let me hear of {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} loyal love, since {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} are the one I rely on. Teach me which road to walk, for my whole being reaches up to {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}.

L.8: Let me hear {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} loyal love in the morning, for in {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} I have trusted; make known to me [the] way [in] which I should walk, for to {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} I lift up my soul.

R.8: In the morning, let me hear about {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} faithful love, because I trust {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}. Show me which way to go, because I long for {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} with all my heart.

decisions.choice: loyal love: faithful, committed love
decisions.reason: The word (chesed) is the love that keeps faith with a bond or covenant. It is "loyal love" at Literal and Balanced and "faithful love" at Readable, as in 5:8.

decisions.choice: in the morning: with the new day, after a night of trouble
decisions.reason: Help comes with the morning (46:6; 90:14).

decisions.choice: lift up my soul: turn my whole desire to you
decisions.reason: As in 25:1 and 86:4, the psalmist turns his whole self toward God in longing and trust.

decisions.choice: my whole being reaches up to you (B); I long for you with all my heart (R)
alternatives: to you I lift up my soul
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what the idiom means (m3).

records.gloss: Deliver me from my enemies, YHWH; to you I have covered.
pieces: Snatch me from my enemies, {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}; I have taken cover with {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}.

L.9: Deliver me from my enemies, {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}; with {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} I have hidden myself.

R.9: {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, save me from my enemies. I have come to {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} to hide.

decisions.choice: I have covered: I have hidden myself with you
alternatives: I have fled to you (the ancient Greek translation)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew (kissiti, "I have covered") is unusual here; it most likely means "I have hidden myself" with God. The ancient Greek translation has "I have fled to you", perhaps from a word that differs by one letter.

decisions.choice: deliver: snatch away, rescue
decisions.reason: The verb (natsal) is to pull someone out of danger (7:2; 142:7).

records.source: לַמְּדֵ֤נִי׀לַֽעֲשׂ֣וֹת רְצוֹנֶךָ֮ כִּֽי־אַתָּ֪ה אֱל֫וֹהָ֥י רוּחֲךָ֥ טוֹבָ֑ה תַּ֝נְחֵ֗נִי בְּאֶ֣רֶץ מִישֽׁוֹר׃
records.gloss: Teach me to do your will, for you [are] my God; your spirit [is] good; may it lead me in a land of level ground.
pieces: Teach me to do what pleases {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, since {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} are my God. May {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} Spirit, who is good, guide me across even ground.

L.10: Teach me to do {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} will, for {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} [are] my God; may {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} good Spirit lead me in a land of level ground.

R.10: Teach me to do what {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} want, because {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} are my God. Let {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} good Spirit lead me on a smooth, safe path.

decisions.choice: your good spirit: God's own Spirit guiding him
decisions.reason: God's spirit is his presence and power at work (51:13; 139:7). Nehemiah 9:20 also speaks of the "good spirit" God gave to instruct Israel. As in 51:13, it is capitalized. The words can also be read "your spirit is good; let it lead me".

decisions.choice: a land of level ground: a smooth, safe way
decisions.reason: Level ground is a path without obstacles or traps, a picture of a life kept upright and safe (26:12; 27:11).

decisions.choice: your will: what pleases you
decisions.reason: The word (ratson) is what someone delights in or wants (40:9).

decisions.choice: a smooth, safe path
decisions.reason: Readable explains the picture (m2).

records.source: לְמַֽעַן־שִׁמְךָ֣ יְהוָ֣ה תְּחַיֵּ֑נִי בְּצִדְקָתְךָ֓׀תוֹצִ֖יא מִצָּרָ֣ה נַפְשִֽׁי׃
records.gloss: For the sake of your name, YHWH, you will keep me alive; in your righteousness you will bring out from trouble my soul.
pieces: {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, for the honor of {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} name, keep me alive; in {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} righteousness lead me out of my distress.

L.11: For the sake of {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} name, {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, keep me alive; in {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} righteousness bring my soul out of trouble.

R.11: {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, keep me alive and show everyone what {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} are like. You always do what is right, so bring me out of my trouble.

decisions.choice: for the sake of your name: for your honor
decisions.reason: God's name is his reputation. When he saves those who trust him, people see who he is (23:3; 25:11; 106:8).

decisions.choice: you will keep me alive: a request
decisions.reason: The verbs are in the future form but carry the sense of a prayer, as the rest of the psalm shows.

decisions.choice: show everyone what you are like
alternatives: for the sake of your name
decisions.reason: Readable says what "for your name's sake" means (m1).

decisions.choice: you always do what is right
decisions.reason: As in verse 1.

records.source: וּֽבְחַסְדְּךָ֮ תַּצְמִ֪ית אֹ֫יְבָ֥י וְֽ֭הַאֲבַדְתָּ כָּל־צֹרֲרֵ֣י נַפְשִׁ֑י כִּ֝֗י אֲנִ֣י עַבְדֶּֽךָ׃
records.gloss: And in your loyal love you will destroy my enemies, and you will destroy all [the] foes of my soul, for I [am] your servant.
pieces: In {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} loyal love {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} will put an end to my enemies and wipe out all who attack my life, for I am {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} servant.

L.12: And in {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} loyal love {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} will cut off my enemies and destroy all the foes of my soul, for I [am] {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} servant.

R.12: Because {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} love me faithfully, {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} will destroy my enemies. You will get rid of all who are against me, because I am {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} servant.

decisions.choice: loyal love
decisions.reason: As in 5:8 (chesed).

decisions.choice: you will destroy: a confident prayer
decisions.reason: As in verse 11, the verbs can be read as requests or as the confidence that God will act. Either way the psalmist leaves his enemies to God.

decisions.choice: your servant: one who belongs to God and serves him
decisions.reason: As in verse 2, the psalmist calls himself God's servant ('eved), one who belongs to him and looks to him for protection (116:16).
